attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Memory — nlp_variance_gtheory
2	
3	## Gated Model 约束 (2026-05-20)
4	Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 和 gemma-2-9b-it 是 HF gated models，直接用 repo ID 加载失败。westd-32570 上通过 ModelScope 下载到本地路径（如 `/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache/LLM-Research/Meta-Llama-3___1-8B-Instruct`）。exp-001 正式运行需要 model path mapping 或 HF token。
5	
6	## 双 Metric 设计决策 (2026-05-20, D002)
7	binary_correct 和 text_exact_match 测量正交维度（Spearman ρ = −0.21, n.s.）。前者衡量评估有效性（item 难度主导），后者衡量可复现性（prompt×item + temperature 主导）。两者必须同时保留——不能互相替代。
8	
9	## Temperature 对 text_match 的决定性影响 (2026-05-20)
10	T=0 → text_match=0.247, T=0.5 → text_match=0.019（降 92%），但 binary_correct 几乎不变。这是 G-theory 框架的关键洞察：采样随机性改变文本表述但不改变答案选择。
11	
12	## FP32 精度效应确认 (2026-05-20)
13	FP32 的 8.5pp accuracy gap 中 97.4% 是精度效应（非引擎 confound）。BF16-trained model 用 FP32 推理表现更差，可能因为权重从 BF16 加载到 FP32 时的数值行为差异。
14	
15	## Gemma2 不支持 float16 (2026-05-21)
16	vLLM 拒绝以 float16 加载 gemma2：`"The model type 'gemma2' does not support float16. Reason: Numerical instability."`。这是架构层面限制，非配置问题。Director 决策 (方案 A 修改版)：cross-model 分析用 bf16+fp32 (2 precisions × 4 models 平衡设计)，fp16 仅用于 Llama/Mistral/Qwen 的 within-model G-study。bf16 vs fp16 差异 <0.1pp (Llama 已证实)，precision 信号集中在 fp32 vs 其他 (10.7pp gap)。
17	
18	## M006: D-study 公式方向性检查 (2026-05-21)
19	D-study 公式 `G_ni = σ²τ / (σ²τ + σ²δ × (n_actual / ni))` — 注意是 n_actual/ni 而非 ni/n_actual。G 必须随 n_items 单调递增（items 越多 error 越小）。所有 D-study 代码必须带 monotonicity assertion。
20	
21	## Cross-model G-study 关键洞察 (2026-05-21, 更新至 8-model)
22	8-model MMLU BF16: item_id=37.88% [33.12, 42.17], model×item=30.21%, G_item=0.896 [0.874, 0.915]。核心叙事 "item difficulty is model-specific" 在 8-model 下仍成立。
23	
24	## G_item 计算 Bug 汇总 (2026-05-21, D016 最终确认)
25	两个独立 bug：(1) gstudy_full.py 用了 ICC 而非 Henderson I G coefficient；(2) FF G-study 代码 residual 除以 1 而非 2304（D016）。统一修复后所有 benchmark G_item 在 0.82-0.90。方差百分比不受影响。
26	
27	## HellaSwag 3-temp Bug (2026-05-22)
28	`pd.read_json` 解析 JSON `0.7` 为 float64 带精度误差。修复：`.round(1)` before `.astype(str)`。**所有跨 benchmark 比较必须用 2-temp 数据**。
29	
30	## 8-model Clean 最终数字 (2026-05-22, Phase 2 完成)
31	
32	| Benchmark | Format | item_id% | G_item |
33	|-----------|--------|----------|--------|
34	| MMLU | MC | 37.88% | 0.896 |
35	| ARC | MC | 37.88% | 0.892 |
36	| HellaSwag | MC | 34.27% | 0.872 |
37	| GSM8K | FF | 16.86% | ~0.86 |
38	| MATH | FF | 24.03% | 0.888 |
39	
40	MC mean=36.68%, FF mean=20.45%, diff=16.23pp. Cohen's d=1.73.
41	
42	## D-study 效率比也是 format-conditional 的 (2026-05-22)
43	MC ratio ~11×, FF ratio ~21.5×。Bootstrap CI: 所有 ratio 下界 >10.7×。
44	
45	## D014 叙事验证 (2026-05-22)
46	Cross-benchmark ρ=0.70 (p=0.188), within-MMLU ρ=0.806 (p=0.005)。Format-conditional 是一级叙事，item heterogeneity 是二级机制。
47	
48	## Messing (2026) 引用确认 (2026-05-22)
49	arXiv:2604.11581, Solomon Messing, "Hidden Measurement Error in LLM Pipelines Distorts Annotation, Evaluation, and Benchmarking"。使用 G-theory，judge identity 43.8%, prompt×judge 12.4% — 两个数字都准确。之前因拼写 "Mesting" 误报为幻觉。
50	
51	## Scale Validation 初步结论 (2026-05-22, Phase 3)
52	Qwen2.5 within-family 3-point scale validation (MMLU, bf16×2temp, 5-facet Henderson I):
53	- **3B**: item_id=75.3%, G_item=0.963, accuracy=0.682
54	- **7B**: item_id=73.4%, G_item=0.956, accuracy=0.742
55	- **ref (Llama-8B bf16×2t)**: item_id=68.5%, G_item=0.937
56	- 结论：item dominance 在 3B-7B range 内是 scale-invariant，甚至比 8B 更强
57	- 7B 对 prompt wording 更敏感（prompt:item=12.2% vs 3B 的 8.8%）
58	- 72B 待完成（下载中 ~19/140GB）

binary_correct 和 text_exact_match 测量正交维度（Spearman ρ = −0.21, n.s.）。前者衡量评估有效性（item 难度主导），后者衡量可复现性（prompt×item + temperature 主导）。两者必须同时保留——不能互相替代。

## Temperature 对 text_match 的决定性影响 (2026-05-20)
T=0 → text_match=0.247, T=0.5 → text_match=0.019（降 92%），但 binary_correct 几乎不变。这是 G-theory 框架的关键洞察：采样随机性改变文本表述但不改变答案选择。

## FP32 精度效应确认 (2026-05-20)
FP32 的 8.5pp accuracy gap 中 97.4% 是精度效应（非引擎 confound）。BF16-trained model 用 FP32 推理表现更差，可能因为权重从 BF16 加载到 FP32 时的数值行为差异。

## Gemma2 不支持 float16 (2026-05-21)
vLLM 拒绝以 float16 加载 gemma2：`"The model type 'gemma2' does not support float16. Reason: Numerical instability."`。这是架构层面限制，非配置问题。Director 决策 (方案 A 修改版)：cross-model 分析用 bf16+fp32 (2 precisions × 4 models 平衡设计)，fp16 仅用于 Llama/Mistral/Qwen 的 within-model G-study。bf16 vs fp16 差异 <0.1pp (Llama 已证实)，precision 信号集中在 fp32 vs 其他 (10.7pp gap)。

## M006: D-study 公式方向性检查 (2026-05-21)
D-study 公式 `G_ni = σ²τ / (σ²τ + σ²δ × (n_actual / ni))` — 注意是 n_actual/ni 而非 ni/n_actual。G 必须随 n_items 单调递增（items 越多 error 越小）。所有 D-study 代码必须带 monotonicity assertion。

## Cross-model G-study 关键洞察 (2026-05-21, 更新至 8-model)
8-model MMLU BF16: item_id=37.88% [33.12, 42.17], model×item=30.21%, G_item=0.896 [0.874, 0.915]。核心叙事 "item difficulty is model-specific" 在 8-model 下仍成立。

## G_item 计算 Bug 汇总 (2026-05-21, D016 最终确认)
两个独立 bug：(1) gstudy_full.py 用了 ICC 而非 Henderson I G coefficient；(2) FF G-study 代码 residual 除以 1 而非 2304（D016）。统一修复后所有 benchmark G_item 在 0.82-0.90。方差百分比不受影响。

## HellaSwag 3-temp Bug (2026-05-22)
`pd.read_json` 解析 JSON `0.7` 为 float64 带精度误差。修复：`.round(1)` before `.astype(str)`。**所有跨 benchmark 比较必须用 2-temp 数据**。

## 8-model Clean 最终数字 (2026-05-22, Phase 2 完成)

| Benchmark | Format | item_id% | G_item |
|-----------|--------|----------|--------|
| MMLU | MC | 37.88% | 0.896 |
| ARC | MC | 37.88% | 0.892 |
| HellaSwag | MC | 34.27% | 0.872 |
| GSM8K | FF | 16.86% | ~0.86 |
| MATH | FF | 24.03% | 0.888 |

MC mean=36.68%, FF mean=20.45%, diff=16.23pp. Cohen's d=1.73.

## D-study 效率比也是 format-conditional 的 (2026-05-22)
MC ratio ~11×, FF ratio ~21.5×。Bootstrap CI: 所有 ratio 下界 >10.7×。

## D014 叙事验证 (2026-05-22)
Cross-benchmark ρ=0.70 (p=0.188), within-MMLU ρ=0.806 (p=0.005)。Format-conditional 是一级叙事，item heterogeneity 是二级机制。

## Messing (2026) 引用确认 (2026-05-22)
arXiv:2604.11581, Solomon Messing, "Hidden Measurement Error in LLM Pipelines Distorts Annotation, Evaluation, and Benchmarking"。使用 G-theory，judge identity 43.8%, prompt×judge 12.4% — 两个数字都准确。之前因拼写 "Mesting" 误报为幻觉。

## Scale Validation 初步结论 (2026-05-22, Phase 3)
Qwen2.5 within-family 3-point scale validation (MMLU, bf16×2temp, 5-facet Henderson I):
- **3B**: item_id=75.3%, G_item=0.963, accuracy=0.682
- **7B**: item_id=73.4%, G_item=0.956, accuracy=0.742
- **ref (Llama-8B bf16×2t)**: item_id=68.5%, G_item=0.937
- 结论：item dominance 在 3B-7B range 内是 scale-invariant，甚至比 8B 更强
- 7B 对 prompt wording 更敏感（prompt:item=12.2% vs 3B 的 8.8%）
- 72B 待完成（下载中 ~19/140GB）

1	# Paper Framing — nlp_variance_gtheory
2	
3	## Target Venue
4	- Primary: EMNLP 2026 via ARR (submission deadline 2026-05-25)

6	- Extended: TACL (rolling)

8	## Title
9	Reproducibility Budgets for LLM Evaluation: A Generalizability Theory Analysis of Variance Sources Across Benchmarks, Models, and Evaluation Metrics
10	
11	## Core Claims (3 条，可证伪)
12	
13	**Claim 1 — Format-Associated Item-Related Variance Concentration**: LLM evaluation variance structure shows a format-associated pattern. We define **item-related variance** = item main effect + model×item interaction (DIF: differential item functioning — model-specific item difficulty). MC benchmarks concentrate item-related variance: MMLU 68.1%, ARC 71.6%, HellaSwag 70.3% (all >67%). FF benchmarks disperse it: GSM8K 31.5%, MATH 41.3% (all <42%). Gap 26.8pp with no overlap across all 5 benchmarks. The mechanism is item difficulty heterogeneity: within MMLU's 57 subjects, subjects with higher item difficulty dispersion show higher item variance (ρ=0.806, p=0.005). This structural difference implies different optimization strategies but does NOT predict item budgets — 8-model n(G≥0.80): ARC(MC) 98 < MATH(FF) 101 < HellaSwag(MC) 118 < GSM8K(FF) 128, MC/FF completely interleaved. Cohen's d=1.73 (n=5, permutation p=0.10 = mathematical floor for C(5,3)=10 partitions — report as observed pattern, not statistical conclusion).
14	**Reframing rationale (D017)**: Previous "item dominates in MC" fails for HellaSwag (item 34.3% < m×i 36.0%). R1 suggested aggregating item+m×i as "item-related" — psychometrically justified via DIF literature (Brennan 2001 Ch.4, Embretson & Reise 2000). Must front-load this definition in Method section as original design concept, not reactive patch.
15	**Three-level narrative**: (1) item-related variance CONCENTRATION is format-associated (observed pattern, strong descriptive evidence); (2) optimization STRATEGY differs by format (inference); (3) item BUDGET is NOT format-associated (don't claim).
16	**Cross-model finding (exp-001)**: Item_id drops from 61% (single-model) to 42% (cross-model) as model×item (34%) absorbs model-conditional difficulty. Item difficulty rankings are model-specific — single-model G-studies overestimate item dominance by conflating universal and model-specific difficulty.
17	**Cross-benchmark finding (exp-004, 8 models × 5 benchmarks, 2,304,000 records)**: MC benchmarks internally consistent (item_id 34-38%), FF benchmarks lower (17-24%). MMLU and ARC converge to identical 37.88% at 8 models. The structural shift is between evaluation formats; within-MMLU gradient (ρ=0.806) confirms item heterogeneity as mechanism.
18	**Empirical anchors (exp-001, 4 models, balanced bf16, 345,600 records)**: Single-model item_id=61.1%, cross-model item_id=42.1% [36.0-48.8%] (↓19pp), model×item=33.6% [28.4-37.9%] (second-largest source, increased from 3-model 31.7%). G_item=0.820 [0.782-0.861]. D-study prediction validated out-of-sample: 3-model predicted G=0.816 for n=4, actual=0.820 (Δ=0.004). Forward projection: 5 models → G=0.848, 8→0.893, 10→0.910 (G≥0.90 requires ~10 models). Residual dropped 24%→19.5% as 4th model split residual into model×item. Per-model interaction: Mistral 29.25% (lowest accuracy 63.8%) > Qwen 27.11% > Gemma 23.95% > Llama 19.69%.
19	**REML robustness**: REML-EM (500 iter, practical convergence Δ<0.003pp) confirms Henderson I: all components differ <0.5pp. Henderson I unbiased for balanced designs. Dataset B differences (item_id 38→52%, model×item 26→12%) due to design differences (factor selection), not estimator bias — measurement design choices themselves affect observed variance structure.
20	**Completed robustness**: BF16-vs-FP16 sensitivity confirms precision→0.0006% without FP32 (FP32 is sole source of precision variance); leave-one-model-out (matched-spec) shows G_item range 0.747-0.793 across 3-model subsets (spread=0.046) — all below 0.80, confirming 4 models is the minimum for reliable cross-model measurement. LOMO also confirms item_id dominance and model×item as second-largest source are stable across all subsets.
21	**GLMM cross-check (dual-analysis, must report both)**: Two complementary analyses:
22	(i) *Marginal logit ANOVA*: All 7 grouped component rankings preserved exactly (ρ=1.0), consistent with MQL-1 prediction that logit-scaling is approximately constant at p̄=0.70.
23	(ii) *VB GLMM (25-item subsample)*: Ranking reversal on top-2 — model:item_id=47.3% > item_id=22.8% on logit scale (ρ=0.571, p=0.18). Attributable to model underspecification (missing 4 item-interaction terms in VB model) + subsample.
24	**Paper must present BOTH honestly** — "marginal logit ANOVA preserves all rankings; VB GLMM shows differences attributable to model underspecification." Do NOT overwrite ρ=0.571 with ρ=1.0. Implication: model×item interaction may be even more important than Henderson I indicates on logit scale — strengthens Claim 1's core message.
25	
26	**Claim 2 — Conditional Separability**: Infrastructure factors (numerical precision) and methodology factors (prompt, seed, temperature, ordering) are approximately separable at the aggregate level — direct infrastructure×methodology interaction ≈0% under binary scoring; the only detectable cross-factor interaction (precision×temperature=1.3%) emerges under text-exact-match scoring, consistent with floating-point non-associativity (Messina & Scotta, 2026). Both factor types interact substantially with item difficulty (precision×item, prompt×item), making their effects item-conditional. This provides a metric-qualified confirmatory finding for isolated-factor studies while warning that conclusions are conditional on item selection and evaluation metric. Note: with only numerical precision tested on a single GPU architecture (pending exp-003 for hardware crossing), "infrastructure" is currently limited to the precision facet.
27	
28	**Claim 3 — Design-Dependent Reproducibility Budget**: Reproducibility budgets are fundamentally design-dependent. The critical insight: the number of items needed for reliable measurement depends dramatically on how many evaluation conditions you use.
29	- **Multi-facet design** (8 models × 6 prompts × 6 seeds × 2 temps × 4 orderings = 1,296 conditions/item): G=0.936 at 200 items, G≥0.80 at only **55 items**.
30	- **Single-condition evaluation** (1×1×1×1, typical practice): G=0.592 at 200 items, G≥0.80 requires **552 items**.
31	- **Partial design** (4 conditions): G≥0.80 requires **245 items** (4.5× multi-facet).
32	- **IRT's 116-item recommendation** yields G=0.457 under single-condition — far below the 0.80 reliability threshold. IRT ignores prompt, seed, and ordering facets entirely.
33	The **10.0× efficiency gap** between multi-facet (55 items) and single-condition (552 items) is the core practical contribution: G-theory shows that **investing in evaluation conditions is more efficient than adding items** when prompt/seed/ordering facets contribute substantial variance.
34	
35	## Contributions (restructured per review: 2 core + 2 auxiliary)
36	
37	### Core Contributions
38	
39	1. **Format-associated item-related variance concentration + item heterogeneity mechanism**: In a crossed 8-model × 5-benchmark design (2,304,000 records), item-related variance (item + model×item DIF) concentrates in MC benchmarks (68-72%) and disperses in FF benchmarks (31-41%), with no overlap across all 5 benchmarks. G_item is uniformly high across all formats (0.86-0.90 with multi-facet formula). The mechanism is item difficulty heterogeneity: within-MMLU gradient shows ρ=0.806 (p=0.005) between std(p_i) and item variance share. [Note: contribution is the format-associated concentration pattern + mechanism identification. "item-related" aggregation justified by DIF literature (Brennan 2001, Embretson & Reise 2000). Model×item = differential item functioning, operationally an item property. Must NOT use "hidden" — model×item known in IRT literature.]
40	
41	2. **Design-dependent reproducibility budgets via D-study**: The first empirical quantification of how evaluation design choices affect measurement reliability in LLM evaluation. Single-condition evaluation (typical practice) requires **552 items** for G≥0.80; a multi-facet design reduces this to **55 items** — an approximately **10× efficiency gain** from condition averaging (bootstrap CI pending). G-theory's D-study reveals this tradeoff explicitly: investing in evaluation conditions is more efficient than adding items. The practical implication: current evaluation practices (1 prompt, 1 seed, ~200 items) achieve G=0.592 — the field is in a reliability gap it cannot see without multi-facet analysis. [Note: IRT comparison is illustrative only (different optimization objectives); label explicitly as such.]
42	
43	### Auxiliary Findings
44	
45	3. **Precision separability (confirmatory)**: BF16/FP16 interchangeable under binary scoring (<0.1% interaction). Confirmatory null result with direct practical value for evaluation practitioners. [Demoted from core contribution per reviewer consensus.]

49	## Methodological Robustness Package (6 验证分析)
50	All completed on Llama 239,200 records:
51	- **Binary data not artifact**: Null simulation item_id=0.08% vs observed 61.1% (737.5×); obs/Bernoulli ratio=1.0008
52	- **Fixed vs random insensitive**: G_item difference only 0.37pp (all-random 0.820 vs fixed temp+ordering 0.824); facet classification near-insensitive
53	- **Bootstrap = jackknife**: CI width ratio 0.96-1.04, independence violation negligible
54	- **Temperature stratification**: Binary G degrades T=0.0 (0.760) → T=0.7 (0.549); text metric unreliable at all T>0
55	- **D-study formula verified (8-model, Henderson I)**: Multi-facet min_items_G80=55, single-condition min_items_G80=552, ratio **10.0×**. G@200: multi-facet 0.936, single-condition 0.592. Progressive validation: ratio stable across 4-model (8.8×) and 8-model (10.0×) designs. Paper reports 10.0× as the 8-model definitive result.
56	- **IRT comparison (8-model)**: IRT's 116 items → G=0.457 under single-condition (insufficient). Single-condition G-theory needs 552 items (4.8× IRT). Multi-facet G-theory needs only 55 items (0.47× IRT). The 10.0× gap quantifies the value of multi-facet design.
57	- **REML vs Henderson I**: REML-EM (500 iter) confirms all components within <0.5pp of Henderson I; Henderson I unbiased for balanced designs

G_item range 0.747-0.793 (spread=0.046), all below 0.80 — confirming 4 models is the minimum configuration for G≥0.80. This strengthens the D-study "need ~10 models for G≥0.90" prediction.

63	## Story Spine
64	
65	**Problem**: When LLM evaluation results vary across reproductions, practitioners cannot determine whether the culprit is prompt phrasing, random seed, GPU hardware, numerical precision, temperature, or item selection — let alone how these factors interact. Every prior study isolates at most two sources, implicitly assuming separability.
66	
67	**Existing approaches & gaps**: Bouthillier et al. (2021) decomposed ML benchmark variance across hyperparameters, data splits, and seeds via ANOVA, establishing the template for factorial variance decomposition in ML evaluation. Mesting (2026) adapted G-theory to 5 methodological facets in LLM evaluation but treated infrastructure as fixed. Yuan et al. (2025) documented up to 9% accuracy variation from hardware/precision without factorial attribution. Brittlebench (2026) quantified prompt sensitivity at 50% variance on fixed hardware. IRT-based approaches (Lalor et al. 2019; Rodriguez et al. 2021; Polo et al. 2024) have analyzed item-level properties and efficient subsampling, but from a different methodological perspective than G-theory. No study has: (a) crossed infrastructure and methodology in a unified G-theory framework, (b) compared variance structure across multiple benchmarks, or (c) provided metric-conditional reproducibility budgets.
68	
69	**Our framing**: We conduct a multi-benchmark G-theory study crossing infrastructure (numerical precision) × methodology (prompt, seed, temperature, ordering) × measurement (item) factors, with model treated as a crossed quasi-random facet (8 models from 6 architecture families). The infrastructure crossing yields a confirmatory null result: aggregate separability holds. The primary novel finding is a **format-conditional variance structure**: MC tasks (ARC/HellaSwag/MMLU) concentrate variance in items (34-38%), while free-form reasoning tasks (GSM8K/MATH) distribute it across model, prompt, and item facets (17-24% item_id). The mechanism is item difficulty heterogeneity (within-MMLU gradient ρ=0.806, p=0.005). This structural difference implies format-specific optimization strategies but — critically — does NOT predict item budgets (HellaSwag MC needs the most items of all benchmarks). D-study projections provide the first benchmark-specific, design-dependent reproducibility budgets, revealing a 10.0× efficiency gap between multi-facet and single-condition designs (55 vs 552 items for G≥0.80).
70	
71	**Headline result template**: "In a G-study of 2,304,000 evaluation records across 8 models and 5 benchmarks (200 items × 6 prompts × 6 seeds × 2 temperatures × 4 orderings), item selection accounts for 34-38% of MC variance but only 17-24% of free-form variance (Cohen's d=1.73). The mechanism is item difficulty heterogeneity (within-MMLU ρ=0.806, p=0.005). Multi-facet G_item is uniformly high (0.86-0.90) across all formats. D-study projections reveal a 10.0× design efficiency gap: a multi-facet design needs only 55 items for G≥0.80, while single-condition evaluation needs 552 items — IRT's recommended 116 items yields only G=0.457 under typical practice. BF16 and FP16 are interchangeable under binary scoring (<0.1% interaction). We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and D-study budget calculator."

73	## Hook (Counter-Intuitive Quantified Claim)
74	"Multiple-choice and free-form LLM benchmarks have fundamentally different variance structures: on MC tasks, item selection drives 34-38% of variance while prompt wording is negligible (<3%); on reasoning tasks like GSM8K, model×prompt interaction alone accounts for ~9% of variance — models respond differently to prompt changes, and residual variance reaches 40%. Yet reliability (G≥0.86) is uniformly high when using multi-facet designs — the difference is WHERE to optimize, not WHETHER reliability is achievable. A 10× efficiency gap separates multi-facet from single-condition evaluation design."

76	## Narrative Strategy

78	- **Tension**: "No universal recipe" — the field seeks standardization but variance structure varies qualitatively across task types
79	- **Intro structure**: 4 paragraphs + 3 contributions (field mode from distilled writing patterns)

88	  - Infrastructure crossing framed as **confirmatory** (validates isolated-factor studies), not as primary novelty
89	  - Item dominance acknowledged as **psychometrically expected**; contribution is quantification + benchmark gradient

Permutation p=0.10 at n=5 floor — report effect size not significance. Three-level narrative distinguishes structure (claim) from strategy (inference) from budget (don't claim)

109	10. **"Incremental over Mesting (2026)"** → Infrastructure crossing is confirmatory (valuable as validation, not breakthrough). Primary novelty: cross-benchmark gradient, task-specific budgets, dual-metric analysis, confound fix. Mesting = single benchmark, no infrastructure; we = multi-benchmark, infrastructure confirmation + benchmark gradient.
110	11. **"Model not treated as G-theory facet"** → exp-004 includes model-as-facet reanalysis of MMLU data. Report model×item interaction separately from residual.
111	12. **"No CIs on variance components"** → exp-004 includes bootstrap CIs (1000 resamples) on all variance components in all tables.

114	15. **"Fine-tuning uses encoder-only RoBERTa"** → Explicitly qualify. Decoder fine-tuning is a natural extension requiring substantially more compute.
115	
116	## Design Decisions
117	- **Judge model fixed**: Unlike Mesting who includes judge as a facet, we fix the judge to isolate infrastructure × methodology interactions. Judge variance (Mesting: 43.8%) would dominate and obscure the effects we study. Adding judge is a natural extension for future work.
118	- **Generation-based evaluation**: Following Hua et al. (EMNLP 2025), we avoid log-likelihood scoring to eliminate scoring artifacts that inflate apparent prompt sensitivity.
119	- **Default vLLM settings**: We use default vLLM settings (without batch-invariant kernels) to reflect realistic practitioner conditions, making CUDA-level nondeterminism a measurable variance source.
120	- **vLLM 0.9.2**: Required for Blackwell GPU (sm_100/sm_120) + CUDA 12.8 support.
121	- **Model as crossed quasi-random facet**: In exp-001 analysis, model is treated as a crossed quasi-random facet — purposive sample from 4 major architecture families (Llama, Gemma, Mistral, Qwen), not a random draw from all LLMs. Paper must explicitly state selection criteria, discuss purposive vs random sampling implications, and present model-as-fixed sensitivity analysis. D-study Δ=0.004 out-of-sample prediction supports exchangeability assumption. Plan to add 2-3 models (Yi-1.5-9B, OLMo-2-7B, etc.) to strengthen to 6-7 models per MF2 resolution.
122	- **Reduced designs for non-MMLU benchmarks**: exp-002 uses 2 precisions × 2 temperatures (vs 3×3 in exp-001) due to GPU budget constraints. Explicitly described as "reduced crossing" rather than "fully crossed."
123	- **Gemma2 float16 exclusion**: Gemma2 architecture does not support float16 inference (vLLM numerical instability guard). Cross-model analysis uses bf16+fp32 (balanced). fp16 data from Llama/Mistral/Qwen used in within-model analyses. bf16≈fp16 difference <0.1pp (D005).
124	
125	## Methodological Defenses (Dream #2 审稿问题逐条应对)
126	
127	### MD1. Binary Data in G-theory
128	**Issue**: Standard G-theory assumes continuous, approximately normal response variables. Binary 0/1 data violates this; item variance is mechanically linked to item difficulty via Bernoulli p(1-p).
129	**Defense strategy (upgraded per Round 1 MF1 + Reviewer + GLMM results)**: Four-line defense, reordered by strength:
130	(a) **PRIMARY — Simulation-based recovery** ✅ DONE (matched design verified): Probit latent model → binary, 100 replications × {50,100,200} items × {0.5-0.8} accuracy. **Strongest finding (matched 1,296-condition design): binary ρ=0.732 ≈ continuous ρ=0.741 at n=200 (Δ=0.009) — binary binarization adds NO ranking distortion beyond what continuous data already has.** Henderson I identifies item_id as #1 systematic source in 99-100% of runs. Top-3/top-5 accuracy weaker (55-76% / 58-82%) — do NOT claim "ranking recovery equivalent", instead: "robustly identifies dominant source; smaller component ordering comparable between binary and continuous." **Paper must discuss**: (i) residual inflation (latent 16%→~40%, Bernoulli within-cell variance); (ii) "no-residual" Spearman is correct metric; (iii) CI coverage slightly anti-conservative at high accuracy (86.4% at p=0.8).
131	(b) **COMPLEMENTARY — GLMM logistic-link**: GLMM (Jiang & Skorupski 2017) on 25-item MMLU subsample showed **ranking reversal**: model:item_id #1 (47.3%) > item_id #2 (22.8%) on logit scale, vs Henderson I item_id #1 (42.1%) > model:item_id #2 (33.6%). Spearman ρ=0.571, p=0.18 — rankings NOT statistically consistent. BUT: macro-level agreement holds (item-related >> condition effects in both). Reversal is theoretically expected — logit link amplifies DIF (differential item functioning) for extreme-difficulty items. **Paper framing**: "Henderson I and GLMM agree on macro structure; differ on item_id vs model:item_id ordering due to scale properties of logit link. This is a complementary perspective, not a contradiction. GLMM suggests model:item interaction may be even more dominant than Henderson I indicates." Do NOT claim GLMM "validates" Henderson I.
132	(c) **Bernoulli-adjusted decomposition**: ✅ DONE. Percentage decomposition inherently normalized by p(1-p) ceiling. Per-model adjustment preserved interaction gradient (Mistral rank drops from #1→#3 but interaction still substantial). Cross-accuracy resampling (0.62-0.72) shows item_id% stable (r=-0.048 with accuracy).
133	(d) **Logprob robustness check**: Continuous metric analysis showing gradient preserved — bypasses binary assumption entirely.
134	(e) **Methods subsection**: "Binary Data Assumptions" discussing Henderson I bias properties for balanced designs, citing Brennan Ch.12, Shavelson et al. 1989, Mushquash & O'Connor 2006, Lalor et al. 2019 (IRT on binary NLP data). Must note GLMM residual drops to 0.004% as Bernoulli variance absorbed by link function.
135	
136	### MD2. Fixed vs Random Facet Sensitivity
137	**Issue**: Temperature (2-3 design points) and ordering (4 systematic rotations) are not randomly sampled from a universe — treating them as random facets may be inappropriate.
138	**Defense ✅ DONE**: All-random G_item=0.820 vs fixed(temp+ordering) G_item=0.824, difference only **0.37pp**. Delta decreases 2.47% when fixing temp+ordering — temperature:item (0.65%) and ordering:item (0.54%) are small enough that fixing these facets barely changes the G coefficient. **Random facet assumption is robust.** REML vs Henderson I comparison also shows <0.5pp difference on all components, confirming estimator choice is insensitive for balanced designs.
139	
140	### MD3. Separability Claim Scope
141	**Issue**: Separability (<0.3%) holds for knowledge benchmarks but not reasoning tasks (GSM8K=3.0%, MATH=2.5%).
142	**Defense**: Qualify all separability claims as "under binary scoring on knowledge-retrieval benchmarks." Present benchmark-conditional separability as a finding (not a limitation): "separability itself varies across task types."
143	
144	### MD4. D-study Optimization Documentation
145	**Issue**: Optimization procedure undocumented; Table 10 arithmetic anomaly (fewer items → higher G).
146	**Defense**: Document grid search procedure (bounds, step sizes, objective function). Verify and explain any non-monotonicity (likely due to joint optimization across facets where reallocating item budget to prompt/seed is more efficient).
147	
148	### MD5. G-coefficient Interpretation
149	**Issue**: G=0.22 for 200 items ≠ "MMLU is unreliable" (standard MMLU uses ~14K items).
150	**Defense**: (a) Clearly distinguish "G for our 200-item subsample design" from "reliability of full MMLU"; (b) Report D-study projection to 14K items; (c) Frame G=0.22 as "cost of subsampling" rather than "MMLU is broken."
151	
152	### MD6. Bootstrap Independence
153	**Issue**: Item-level bootstrap with replacement creates ~127 unique items per 200-item resample, violating independence.
154	**Defense**: (a) Implement delete-1 jackknife as comparison; (b) If bootstrap and jackknife CIs are similar (within 20%), report as robust; (c) Discuss limitation in Methods.
155	
156	### MD7. IRT vs G-theory Comparison
157	**Issue**: tinyBenchmarks recommends ~100 items, D-study recommends 420. 4× discrepancy unexplained.
158	**Defense**: Direct comparison showing G-theory accounts for prompt/seed/ordering dimensions that IRT ignores. The 4× difference is the "cost of multi-facet reliability" — G-theory's budget is larger because it targets reliability across ALL facets, not just items. This comparison is a potential standalone contribution.
159	
160	### MD8. Cross-benchmark Design Asymmetry
161	**Issue**: MMLU uses 3 prec × 3 temp, other benchmarks use 2 × 2.
162	**Defense**: Re-analyze MMLU with matched 2×2 design (bf16/fp16 × T=0.0/T=0.7) and compare variance decomposition. If <5% change, report as robust to design reduction.

164	### MD9. Title-Content Alignment
165	**Issue**: Title promises "Evaluation Metrics" but logprob analysis is minimal.
166	**Defense**: Expand logprob analysis across all benchmarks in exp-004, OR adjust title to "...Across Benchmarks and Models."

# Paper Framing — nlp_variance_gtheory

## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 via ARR (submission deadline 2026-05-25)
- Backup: ACL 2027 via ARR (October 15 cycle)
- Extended: TACL (rolling)

## Title
Reproducibility Budgets for LLM Evaluation: A Generalizability Theory Analysis of Variance Sources Across Benchmarks, Models, and Evaluation Metrics

## Core Claims (3 条，可证伪)

**Claim 1 — Format-Associated Item-Related Variance Concentration**: LLM evaluation variance structure shows a format-associated pattern. We define **item-related variance** = item main effect + model×item interaction (DIF: differential item functioning — model-specific item difficulty). MC benchmarks concentrate item-related variance: MMLU 68.1%, ARC 71.6%, HellaSwag 70.3% (all >67%). FF benchmarks disperse it: GSM8K 31.5%, MATH 41.3% (all <42%). Gap 26.8pp with no overlap across all 5 benchmarks. The mechanism is item difficulty heterogeneity: within MMLU's 57 subjects, subjects with higher item difficulty dispersion show higher item variance (ρ=0.806, p=0.005). This structural difference implies different optimization strategies but does NOT predict item budgets — 8-model n(G≥0.80): ARC(MC) 98 < MATH(FF) 101 < HellaSwag(MC) 118 < GSM8K(FF) 128, MC/FF completely interleaved. Cohen's d=1.73 (n=5, permutation p=0.10 = mathematical floor for C(5,3)=10 partitions — report as observed pattern, not statistical conclusion).
**Reframing rationale (D017)**: Previous "item dominates in MC" fails for HellaSwag (item 34.3% < m×i 36.0%). R1 suggested aggregating item+m×i as "item-related" — psychometrically justified via DIF literature (Brennan 2001 Ch.4, Embretson & Reise 2000). Must front-load this definition in Method section as original design concept, not reactive patch.
**Three-level narrative**: (1) item-related variance CONCENTRATION is format-associated (observed pattern, strong descriptive evidence); (2) optimization STRATEGY differs by format (inference); (3) item BUDGET is NOT format-associated (don't claim).
**Cross-model finding (exp-001)**: Item_id drops from 61% (single-model) to 42% (cross-model) as model×item (34%) absorbs model-conditional difficulty. Item difficulty rankings are model-specific — single-model G-studies overestimate item dominance by conflating universal and model-specific difficulty.
**Cross-benchmark finding (exp-004, 8 models × 5 benchmarks, 2,304,000 records)**: MC benchmarks internally consistent (item_id 34-38%), FF benchmarks lower (17-24%). MMLU and ARC converge to identical 37.88% at 8 models. The structural shift is between evaluation formats; within-MMLU gradient (ρ=0.806) confirms item heterogeneity as mechanism.
**Empirical anchors (exp-001, 4 models, balanced bf16, 345,600 records)**: Single-model item_id=61.1%, cross-model item_id=42.1% [36.0-48.8%] (↓19pp), model×item=33.6% [28.4-37.9%] (second-largest source, increased from 3-model 31.7%). G_item=0.820 [0.782-0.861]. D-study prediction validated out-of-sample: 3-model predicted G=0.816 for n=4, actual=0.820 (Δ=0.004). Forward projection: 5 models → G=0.848, 8→0.893, 10→0.910 (G≥0.90 requires ~10 models). Residual dropped 24%→19.5% as 4th model split residual into model×item. Per-model interaction: Mistral 29.25% (lowest accuracy 63.8%) > Qwen 27.11% > Gemma 23.95% > Llama 19.69%.
**REML robustness**: REML-EM (500 iter, practical convergence Δ<0.003pp) confirms Henderson I: all components differ <0.5pp. Henderson I unbiased for balanced designs. Dataset B differences (item_id 38→52%, model×item 26→12%) due to design differences (factor selection), not estimator bias — measurement design choices themselves affect observed variance structure.
**Completed robustness**: BF16-vs-FP16 sensitivity confirms precision→0.0006% without FP32 (FP32 is sole source of precision variance); leave-one-model-out (matched-spec) shows G_item range 0.747-0.793 across 3-model subsets (spread=0.046) — all below 0.80, confirming 4 models is the minimum for reliable cross-model measurement. LOMO also confirms item_id dominance and model×item as second-largest source are stable across all subsets.
**GLMM cross-check (dual-analysis, must report both)**: Two complementary analyses:
(i) *Marginal logit ANOVA*: All 7 grouped component rankings preserved exactly (ρ=1.0), consistent with MQL-1 prediction that logit-scaling is approximately constant at p̄=0.70.
(ii) *VB GLMM (25-item subsample)*: Ranking reversal on top-2 — model:item_id=47.3% > item_id=22.8% on logit scale (ρ=0.571, p=0.18). Attributable to model underspecification (missing 4 item-interaction terms in VB model) + subsample.
**Paper must present BOTH honestly** — "marginal logit ANOVA preserves all rankings; VB GLMM shows differences attributable to model underspecification." Do NOT overwrite ρ=0.571 with ρ=1.0. Implication: model×item interaction may be even more important than Henderson I indicates on logit scale — strengthens Claim 1's core message.

**Claim 2 — Conditional Separability**: Infrastructure factors (numerical precision) and methodology factors (prompt, seed, temperature, ordering) are approximately separable at the aggregate level — direct infrastructure×methodology interaction ≈0% under binary scoring; the only detectable cross-factor interaction (precision×temperature=1.3%) emerges under text-exact-match scoring, consistent with floating-point non-associativity (Messina & Scotta, 2026). Both factor types interact substantially with item difficulty (precision×item, prompt×item), making their effects item-conditional. This provides a metric-qualified confirmatory finding for isolated-factor studies while warning that conclusions are conditional on item selection and evaluation metric. Note: with only numerical precision tested on a single GPU architecture (pending exp-003 for hardware crossing), "infrastructure" is currently limited to the precision facet.

**Claim 3 — Design-Dependent Reproducibility Budget**: Reproducibility budgets are fundamentally design-dependent. The critical insight: the number of items needed for reliable measurement depends dramatically on how many evaluation conditions you use.
- **Multi-facet design** (8 models × 6 prompts × 6 seeds × 2 temps × 4 orderings = 1,296 conditions/item): G=0.936 at 200 items, G≥0.80 at only **55 items**.
- **Single-condition evaluation** (1×1×1×1, typical practice): G=0.592 at 200 items, G≥0.80 requires **552 items**.
- **Partial design** (4 conditions): G≥0.80 requires **245 items** (4.5× multi-facet).
- **IRT's 116-item recommendation** yields G=0.457 under single-condition — far below the 0.80 reliability threshold. IRT ignores prompt, seed, and ordering facets entirely.
The **10.0× efficiency gap** between multi-facet (55 items) and single-condition (552 items) is the core practical contribution: G-theory shows that **investing in evaluation conditions is more efficient than adding items** when prompt/seed/ordering facets contribute substantial variance.

## Contributions (restructured per review: 2 core + 2 auxiliary)

### Core Contributions

1. **Format-associated item-related variance concentration + item heterogeneity mechanism**: In a crossed 8-model × 5-benchmark design (2,304,000 records), item-related variance (item + model×item DIF) concentrates in MC benchmarks (68-72%) and disperses in FF benchmarks (31-41%), with no overlap across all 5 benchmarks. G_item is uniformly high across all formats (0.86-0.90 with multi-facet formula). The mechanism is item difficulty heterogeneity: within-MMLU gradient shows ρ=0.806 (p=0.005) between std(p_i) and item variance share. [Note: contribution is the format-associated concentration pattern + mechanism identification. "item-related" aggregation justified by DIF literature (Brennan 2001, Embretson & Reise 2000). Model×item = differential item functioning, operationally an item property. Must NOT use "hidden" — model×item known in IRT literature.]

2. **Design-dependent reproducibility budgets via D-study**: The first empirical quantification of how evaluation design choices affect measurement reliability in LLM evaluation. Single-condition evaluation (typical practice) requires **552 items** for G≥0.80; a multi-facet design reduces this to **55 items** — an approximately **10× efficiency gain** from condition averaging (bootstrap CI pending). G-theory's D-study reveals this tradeoff explicitly: investing in evaluation conditions is more efficient than adding items. The practical implication: current evaluation practices (1 prompt, 1 seed, ~200 items) achieve G=0.592 — the field is in a reliability gap it cannot see without multi-facet analysis. [Note: IRT comparison is illustrative only (different optimization objectives); label explicitly as such.]

### Auxiliary Findings

3. **Precision separability (confirmatory)**: BF16/FP16 interchangeable under binary scoring (<0.1% interaction). Confirmatory null result with direct practical value for evaluation practitioners. [Demoted from core contribution per reviewer consensus.]

4. **Practitioner toolkit**: Open-source G-theory variance decomposition pipeline + D-study budget calculator for LLM evaluation.

## Methodological Robustness Package (6 验证分析)
All completed on Llama 239,200 records:
- **Binary data not artifact**: Null simulation item_id=0.08% vs observed 61.1% (737.5×); obs/Bernoulli ratio=1.0008
- **Fixed vs random insensitive**: G_item difference only 0.37pp (all-random 0.820 vs fixed temp+ordering 0.824); facet classification near-insensitive
- **Bootstrap = jackknife**: CI width ratio 0.96-1.04, independence violation negligible
- **Temperature stratification**: Binary G degrades T=0.0 (0.760) → T=0.7 (0.549); text metric unreliable at all T>0
- **D-study formula verified (8-model, Henderson I)**: Multi-facet min_items_G80=55, single-condition min_items_G80=552, ratio **10.0×**. G@200: multi-facet 0.936, single-condition 0.592. Progressive validation: ratio stable across 4-model (8.8×) and 8-model (10.0×) designs. Paper reports 10.0× as the 8-model definitive result.
- **IRT comparison (8-model)**: IRT's 116 items → G=0.457 under single-condition (insufficient). Single-condition G-theory needs 552 items (4.8× IRT). Multi-facet G-theory needs only 55 items (0.47× IRT). The 10.0× gap quantifies the value of multi-facet design.
- **REML vs Henderson I**: REML-EM (500 iter) confirms all components within <0.5pp of Henderson I; Henderson I unbiased for balanced designs
- **D-study uncertainty propagation [Dream A2, TODO]**: Propagate bootstrap CIs on variance components into confidence intervals on D-study budget recommendations (min_items_G80). Currently only point estimates reported; practitioners need uncertainty ranges.
- **Intermediate D-study recommendations [Dream A3, TODO]**: Show what partial improvements buy: "2 prompts × 2 seeds on 200 items → G≈X" to make framework adoptable. Address "20-50× cost" concern from Dream reviewers.
- **BF16-vs-FP16 sensitivity**: Excluding FP32, precision effect drops from 0.4% to 0.0006% (precision×item: 1.3%→0.04%). FP32 anomaly is entirely a vLLM enforce_eager artifact, not a fundamental precision effect. BF16≈FP16 (Δ=0.23pp accuracy)
- **Leave-one-model-out stability**: All 3-model subsets preserve item_id dominance (39-45%) and model×item as second-largest (32-37%). G_item range 0.747-0.793 (spread=0.046), all below 0.80 — confirming 4 models is the minimum configuration for G≥0.80. This strengthens the D-study "need ~10 models for G≥0.90" prediction.

## Story Spine

**Problem**: When LLM evaluation results vary across reproductions, practitioners cannot determine whether the culprit is prompt phrasing, random seed, GPU hardware, numerical precision, temperature, or item selection — let alone how these factors interact. Every prior study isolates at most two sources, implicitly assuming separability.

**Existing approaches & gaps**: Bouthillier et al. (2021) decomposed ML benchmark variance across hyperparameters, data splits, and seeds via ANOVA, establishing the template for factorial variance decomposition in ML evaluation. Mesting (2026) adapted G-theory to 5 methodological facets in LLM evaluation but treated infrastructure as fixed. Yuan et al. (2025) documented up to 9% accuracy variation from hardware/precision without factorial attribution. Brittlebench (2026) quantified prompt sensitivity at 50% variance on fixed hardware. IRT-based approaches (Lalor et al. 2019; Rodriguez et al. 2021; Polo et al. 2024) have analyzed item-level properties and efficient subsampling, but from a different methodological perspective than G-theory. No study has: (a) crossed infrastructure and methodology in a unified G-theory framework, (b) compared variance structure across multiple benchmarks, or (c) provided metric-conditional reproducibility budgets.

**Our framing**: We conduct a multi-benchmark G-theory study crossing infrastructure (numerical precision) × methodology (prompt, seed, temperature, ordering) × measurement (item) factors, with model treated as a crossed quasi-random facet (8 models from 6 architecture families). The infrastructure crossing yields a confirmatory null result: aggregate separability holds. The primary novel finding is a **format-conditional variance structure**: MC tasks (ARC/HellaSwag/MMLU) concentrate variance in items (34-38%), while free-form reasoning tasks (GSM8K/MATH) distribute it across model, prompt, and item facets (17-24% item_id). The mechanism is item difficulty heterogeneity (within-MMLU gradient ρ=0.806, p=0.005). This structural difference implies format-specific optimization strategies but — critically — does NOT predict item budgets (HellaSwag MC needs the most items of all benchmarks). D-study projections provide the first benchmark-specific, design-dependent reproducibility budgets, revealing a 10.0× efficiency gap between multi-facet and single-condition designs (55 vs 552 items for G≥0.80).

**Headline result template**: "In a G-study of 2,304,000 evaluation records across 8 models and 5 benchmarks (200 items × 6 prompts × 6 seeds × 2 temperatures × 4 orderings), item selection accounts for 34-38% of MC variance but only 17-24% of free-form variance (Cohen's d=1.73). The mechanism is item difficulty heterogeneity (within-MMLU ρ=0.806, p=0.005). Multi-facet G_item is uniformly high (0.86-0.90) across all formats. D-study projections reveal a 10.0× design efficiency gap: a multi-facet design needs only 55 items for G≥0.80, while single-condition evaluation needs 552 items — IRT's recommended 116 items yields only G=0.457 under typical practice. BF16 and FP16 are interchangeable under binary scoring (<0.1% interaction). We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and D-study budget calculator."

## Hook (Counter-Intuitive Quantified Claim)
"Multiple-choice and free-form LLM benchmarks have fundamentally different variance structures: on MC tasks, item selection drives 34-38% of variance while prompt wording is negligible (<3%); on reasoning tasks like GSM8K, model×prompt interaction alone accounts for ~9% of variance — models respond differently to prompt changes, and residual variance reaches 40%. Yet reliability (G≥0.86) is uniformly high when using multi-facet designs — the difference is WHERE to optimize, not WHETHER reliability is achievable. A 10× efficiency gap separates multi-facet from single-condition evaluation design."

## Narrative Strategy
- **Type**: Cross-domain transfer (psychometrics G-theory → ML evaluation) + Empirical contribution (benchmark-conditional gradient)
- **Tension**: "No universal recipe" — the field seeks standardization but variance structure varies qualitatively across task types
- **Intro structure**: 4 paragraphs + 3 contributions (field mode from distilled writing patterns)
- **Signature visual**: Stacked-bar variance decomposition chart across benchmarks (field idiom from Mesting/Brittlebench)
- **Figure plan** (5 figures):
  1. **Stacked-bar: single-model vs cross-model variance decomposition** — item_id shrinks from 61% to 42%, model×item appears at 34%, residual drops 24%→20%. The "reveal" figure.
  2. **G-theory crossed design diagram** — facets, levels, crossing structure
  3. **D-study projection curves** — G vs item count for binary (practical vs all-random) and text metric. Shows G≥0.80 threshold at ~414/510 items.
  4. **IRT vs G-theory item requirement comparison** — bar chart showing 116 (IRT) vs 510 (G-theory) items, with breakdown of where the extra items go (prompt×item, seed×item, residual)
  5. **Temperature-stratified G coefficient heatmap** — binary vs text metric × 3 temperatures, showing metric×temperature interaction
- **Key framing shifts from Dream feedback**:
  - Infrastructure crossing framed as **confirmatory** (validates isolated-factor studies), not as primary novelty
  - Item dominance acknowledged as **psychometrically expected**; contribution is quantification + benchmark gradient
  - Cross-benchmark gradient is the **primary novel finding** — 8-model data confirms MC item_id 34-38% vs FF 17-24% with no overlap (d=1.73). MMLU and ARC converge to identical 37.88% — format is the key grouping variable. Within-MMLU gradient (ρ=0.806) confirms item heterogeneity mechanism. Permutation p=0.10 at n=5 floor — report effect size not significance. Three-level narrative distinguishes structure (claim) from strategy (inference) from budget (don't claim)
  - "Fully crossed" language qualified to MMLU exp-001 only; other benchmarks use reduced designs

## Venue Fit Risks
- AAAI: Strong fit for "evaluation methodology" track. Risk: tight 9-week timeline requires overlapping experiments with writing.
- Reviewer concern 1: "Only open-weight models, not API models" — We intentionally study open-weight models where infrastructure is controllable; API models (studied by Mesting) have opaque infrastructure. Frame as complementary.
- Reviewer concern 2: "G-theory is borrowed methodology, not novel" — Frame as cross-domain transfer. The novelty is the cross-benchmark variance gradient finding, not G-theory itself.
- Reviewer concern 3: "Item dominance is obvious from measurement theory" — Acknowledge explicitly. Contribution is quantification (X-Y%, pending exp-001/002), benchmark-dependence, and D-study implications. Contextualize against IRT item analysis literature.

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Planned Responses
1. **"Only N GPU types"** → exp-003 (multi-hardware crossing) addresses this. If blocked, explicitly scope to "numerical precision" and frame hardware as future work.
2. **"float32 engine confound"** → exp-001 fixes with V0 enforce_eager for all precisions. Confound discovery itself is a standalone methodological contribution.
3. **"Only MMLU"** → exp-002 expands to GSM8K, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag. Cross-benchmark gradient is the core finding.
4. **"Small item sample"** → exp-001 expands from 50 to 200 items. exp-001b tests resampling stability.
5. **"No training-time analysis"** → exp-006 (fine-tuning G-study with RoBERTa). Explicitly qualify as encoder-only classification; decoder fine-tuning is future work.
6. **"Missing scale validation"** → exp-005 (14B models)
7. **"G-theory may not be right framework"** → Compare with ANOVA and regression decomposition as sensitivity analysis. Cite Bouthillier et al. (2021) as ANOVA-based predecessor; show G-theory adds D-study projections.
8. **"Separability claim is metric-dependent"** → This is precisely the point: reproducibility budgets must be metric-qualified. Replace arbitrary threshold with bootstrap CI on interaction term.
9. **"FP32 degradation is already known (Yuan 2025)"** → Position as supporting finding with novel item-level breakdown. Not an independent claim.
10. **"Incremental over Mesting (2026)"** → Infrastructure crossing is confirmatory (valuable as validation, not breakthrough). Primary novelty: cross-benchmark gradient, task-specific budgets, dual-metric analysis, confound fix. Mesting = single benchmark, no infrastructure; we = multi-benchmark, infrastructure confirmation + benchmark gradient.
11. **"Model not treated as G-theory facet"** → exp-004 includes model-as-facet reanalysis of MMLU data. Report model×item interaction separately from residual.
12. **"No CIs on variance components"** → exp-004 includes bootstrap CIs (1000 resamples) on all variance components in all tables.
13. **"Missing related work — IRT, tinyBenchmarks, Bouthillier"** → Comprehensive bibliography (25+ refs). Position D-study budgets against IRT-based subsampling. Cite Bouthillier et al. as ANOVA predecessor.
14. **"Diagnostic tool claim unsubstantiated"** → Release analysis pipeline code (G-theory variance decomposition + D-study projections) as reusable tool. Or reframe as "empirical analysis + data release."
15. **"Fine-tuning uses encoder-only RoBERTa"** → Explicitly qualify. Decoder fine-tuning is a natural extension requiring substantially more compute.

## Design Decisions
- **Judge model fixed**: Unlike Mesting who includes judge as a facet, we fix the judge to isolate infrastructure × methodology interactions. Judge variance (Mesting: 43.8%) would dominate and obscure the effects we study. Adding judge is a natural extension for future work.
- **Generation-based evaluation**: Following Hua et al. (EMNLP 2025), we avoid log-likelihood scoring to eliminate scoring artifacts that inflate apparent prompt sensitivity.
- **Default vLLM settings**: We use default vLLM settings (without batch-invariant kernels) to reflect realistic practitioner conditions, making CUDA-level nondeterminism a measurable variance source.
- **vLLM 0.9.2**: Required for Blackwell GPU (sm_100/sm_120) + CUDA 12.8 support.
- **Model as crossed quasi-random facet**: In exp-001 analysis, model is treated as a crossed quasi-random facet — purposive sample from 4 major architecture families (Llama, Gemma, Mistral, Qwen), not a random draw from all LLMs. Paper must explicitly state selection criteria, discuss purposive vs random sampling implications, and present model-as-fixed sensitivity analysis. D-study Δ=0.004 out-of-sample prediction supports exchangeability assumption. Plan to add 2-3 models (Yi-1.5-9B, OLMo-2-7B, etc.) to strengthen to 6-7 models per MF2 resolution.
- **Reduced designs for non-MMLU benchmarks**: exp-002 uses 2 precisions × 2 temperatures (vs 3×3 in exp-001) due to GPU budget constraints. Explicitly described as "reduced crossing" rather than "fully crossed."
- **Gemma2 float16 exclusion**: Gemma2 architecture does not support float16 inference (vLLM numerical instability guard). Cross-model analysis uses bf16+fp32 (balanced). fp16 data from Llama/Mistral/Qwen used in within-model analyses. bf16≈fp16 difference <0.1pp (D005).

## Methodological Defenses (Dream #2 审稿问题逐条应对)

### MD1. Binary Data in G-theory
**Issue**: Standard G-theory assumes continuous, approximately normal response variables. Binary 0/1 data violates this; item variance is mechanically linked to item difficulty via Bernoulli p(1-p).
**Defense strategy (upgraded per Round 1 MF1 + Reviewer + GLMM results)**: Four-line defense, reordered by strength:
(a) **PRIMARY — Simulation-based recovery** ✅ DONE (matched design verified): Probit latent model → binary, 100 replications × {50,100,200} items × {0.5-0.8} accuracy. **Strongest finding (matched 1,296-condition design): binary ρ=0.732 ≈ continuous ρ=0.741 at n=200 (Δ=0.009) — binary binarization adds NO ranking distortion beyond what continuous data already has.** Henderson I identifies item_id as #1 systematic source in 99-100% of runs. Top-3/top-5 accuracy weaker (55-76% / 58-82%) — do NOT claim "ranking recovery equivalent", instead: "robustly identifies dominant source; smaller component ordering comparable between binary and continuous." **Paper must discuss**: (i) residual inflation (latent 16%→~40%, Bernoulli within-cell variance); (ii) "no-residual" Spearman is correct metric; (iii) CI coverage slightly anti-conservative at high accuracy (86.4% at p=0.8).
(b) **COMPLEMENTARY — GLMM logistic-link**: GLMM (Jiang & Skorupski 2017) on 25-item MMLU subsample showed **ranking reversal**: model:item_id #1 (47.3%) > item_id #2 (22.8%) on logit scale, vs Henderson I item_id #1 (42.1%) > model:item_id #2 (33.6%). Spearman ρ=0.571, p=0.18 — rankings NOT statistically consistent. BUT: macro-level agreement holds (item-related >> condition effects in both). Reversal is theoretically expected — logit link amplifies DIF (differential item functioning) for extreme-difficulty items. **Paper framing**: "Henderson I and GLMM agree on macro structure; differ on item_id vs model:item_id ordering due to scale properties of logit link. This is a complementary perspective, not a contradiction. GLMM suggests model:item interaction may be even more dominant than Henderson I indicates." Do NOT claim GLMM "validates" Henderson I.
(c) **Bernoulli-adjusted decomposition**: ✅ DONE. Percentage decomposition inherently normalized by p(1-p) ceiling. Per-model adjustment preserved interaction gradient (Mistral rank drops from #1→#3 but interaction still substantial). Cross-accuracy resampling (0.62-0.72) shows item_id% stable (r=-0.048 with accuracy).
(d) **Logprob robustness check**: Continuous metric analysis showing gradient preserved — bypasses binary assumption entirely.
(e) **Methods subsection**: "Binary Data Assumptions" discussing Henderson I bias properties for balanced designs, citing Brennan Ch.12, Shavelson et al. 1989, Mushquash & O'Connor 2006, Lalor et al. 2019 (IRT on binary NLP data). Must note GLMM residual drops to 0.004% as Bernoulli variance absorbed by link function.

### MD2. Fixed vs Random Facet Sensitivity
**Issue**: Temperature (2-3 design points) and ordering (4 systematic rotations) are not randomly sampled from a universe — treating them as random facets may be inappropriate.
**Defense ✅ DONE**: All-random G_item=0.820 vs fixed(temp+ordering) G_item=0.824, difference only **0.37pp**. Delta decreases 2.47% when fixing temp+ordering — temperature:item (0.65%) and ordering:item (0.54%) are small enough that fixing these facets barely changes the G coefficient. **Random facet assumption is robust.** REML vs Henderson I comparison also shows <0.5pp difference on all components, confirming estimator choice is insensitive for balanced designs.

### MD3. Separability Claim Scope
**Issue**: Separability (<0.3%) holds for knowledge benchmarks but not reasoning tasks (GSM8K=3.0%, MATH=2.5%).
**Defense**: Qualify all separability claims as "under binary scoring on knowledge-retrieval benchmarks." Present benchmark-conditional separability as a finding (not a limitation): "separability itself varies across task types."

### MD4. D-study Optimization Documentation
**Issue**: Optimization procedure undocumented; Table 10 arithmetic anomaly (fewer items → higher G).
**Defense**: Document grid search procedure (bounds, step sizes, objective function). Verify and explain any non-monotonicity (likely due to joint optimization across facets where reallocating item budget to prompt/seed is more efficient).

### MD5. G-coefficient Interpretation
**Issue**: G=0.22 for 200 items ≠ "MMLU is unreliable" (standard MMLU uses ~14K items).
**Defense**: (a) Clearly distinguish "G for our 200-item subsample design" from "reliability of full MMLU"; (b) Report D-study projection to 14K items; (c) Frame G=0.22 as "cost of subsampling" rather than "MMLU is broken."

### MD6. Bootstrap Independence
**Issue**: Item-level bootstrap with replacement creates ~127 unique items per 200-item resample, violating independence.
**Defense**: (a) Implement delete-1 jackknife as comparison; (b) If bootstrap and jackknife CIs are similar (within 20%), report as robust; (c) Discuss limitation in Methods.

### MD7. IRT vs G-theory Comparison
**Issue**: tinyBenchmarks recommends ~100 items, D-study recommends 420. 4× discrepancy unexplained.
**Defense**: Direct comparison showing G-theory accounts for prompt/seed/ordering dimensions that IRT ignores. The 4× difference is the "cost of multi-facet reliability" — G-theory's budget is larger because it targets reliability across ALL facets, not just items. This comparison is a potential standalone contribution.

### MD8. Cross-benchmark Design Asymmetry
**Issue**: MMLU uses 3 prec × 3 temp, other benchmarks use 2 × 2.
**Defense**: Re-analyze MMLU with matched 2×2 design (bf16/fp16 × T=0.0/T=0.7) and compare variance decomposition. If <5% change, report as robust to design reduction.

### MD9. Title-Content Alignment
**Issue**: Title promises "Evaluation Metrics" but logprob analysis is minimal.
**Defense**: Expand logprob analysis across all benchmarks in exp-004, OR adjust title to "...Across Benchmarks and Models."

## Required Bibliography (minimum 25 references)
Key references to include beyond current literature_map:
- Bouthillier et al. (2021, JMLR) — ML variance decomposition via ANOVA
- Lalor et al. (2019, NAACL) — IRT-based item analysis in NLP
- Rodriguez et al. (2021, ACL) — IRT evaluation for NLP
- Polo et al. (2024) — tinyBenchmarks, IRT-based subsampling
- Perlitz et al. (2023) — Efficient LLM benchmarking
- Henderson et al. (2018) — Deep RL reproducibility, variance decomposition
- Shavelson & Webb (1991) — G-theory primer (canonical)
- Brennan (2001) — G-theory textbook (canonical, Ch.12 on binary data)
- Lu et al. (2022) — Option ordering effects in MC evaluation
- Pezeshkpour & Hruschka (2024) — Option ordering effects
- Dodge et al. (2020, EMNLP) — Fine-tuning instability (seed, data order)
- Sellam et al. (2022) — MultiBERTs, multi-seed training
- Dehghani et al. (2021) — Benchmark Lottery
- Biderman et al. (2024) — Evaluation reproducibility lessons
- Vania et al. (2021) — IRT item properties in NLP
- **Sclar et al. (2024, ICLR)** — Up to 76% accuracy swing from prompt formatting; directly relevant to prompt×item variance [Dream #3: all 3 tiers flagged as missing]
- **Kunievsky & Evans (2025)** — Alternative decomposition: intent/articulation/model uncertainty; competing framework to G-theory [Dream #3: all 3 tiers flagged]
- **Bui et al. (2025)** — Extreme seed sensitivity in fine-tuning (RTES variance=18.22 for RoBERTa on COPA) [Dream #3: relevant to exp-006]
- **Jiang & Skorupski (2017)** — Logistic-link generalized G-theory for binary data [Dream #3 worst: methodological defense for REML on binary]
- **Mushquash & O'Connor (2006)** — Binary-data G-theory [Dream #3: classical psychometrics gap]
- **Shavelson et al. (1989)** — Binary response G-theory treatment [Dream #3: classical psychometrics]

## Dream #3 Framing Directives (2026-05-21, D006)
Post-analysis framing adjustments based on three-tier consistent feedback:
1. **Center gradient + model×item as primary contributions** — infrastructure crossing is confirmatory secondary
2. **Position explicitly as empirical extension of Mesting (2026)** with novel findings (model×item quantification, D-study out-of-sample validation, IRT comparison), not a new framework. Remove "first" claims where not defensible.
3. **Scope Claim 2 to "precision separability"** — not "infrastructure" broadly. Single GPU architecture.
4. **Item dominance is psychometrically expected** — contribution is quantification of magnitude, metric-conditionality, and D-study implications
5. **Fine-tuning (exp-006) downgraded** to Discussion-section preliminary observation, not a numbered contribution
6. **Add explicit judge-facet exclusion discussion** vs Mesting: we fix judge to isolate other factors; Mesting's 43.8% judge variance would dominate
7. **Practitioner toolkit must be concrete**: specify released scripts, D-study calculator, budget lookup tables
8. **Figures are non-negotiable**: 5 planned figures address all-tier "zero figures" criticism

## Dream #4 Framing Directives (2026-05-21, D008)
Post-analysis adjustments based on Dream #4 (best 7, median 6, worst 5):
1. **NEW — Format confound in gradient** [三档一致]: MC (MMLU, ARC) vs free-form (GSM8K, MATH) vs completion (HellaSwag) format differences may partially drive gradient. Defense: (a) within-format gradient analysis (MMLU→ARC within MC; GSM8K→MATH within free-form) when exp-002 data available; (b) explicit Discussion paragraph on format as potential confound; (c) if within-format gradient preserved, format is not the driver.
2. **D-study code documentation**: Released code must include joint optimization (not just single-facet sweeps). Fix before submission.
3. **Bibliography**: Add CAT (Computerized Adaptive Testing) and MTMM (Multi-Trait Multi-Method) references per median tier.
4. **Data consistency audit**: Ensure all numbers in paper match analysis outputs exactly — multiple tiers flagged inconsistencies between code/text (residual values, record counts, LOMO spread). Pre-submission checklist item.
5. **Sclar et al. discrepancy**: Our prompt×item is 3.8-4.6% vs Sclar's 76% accuracy swing. Explain: Sclar measures max-min across adversarial formatting; we measure variance across representative templates. Different questions, compatible answers.

_next_id: 31
mistakes:
- id: M001
  date: '2026-05-20'
  category: agent_behavior
  severity: medium
  summary: Agent 代码部署后空闲 40 分钟未启动数据生成，因 CPU 依赖缺失未及时处理
  root_cause: 代码部署 Worker 发现 datasets/pandas 未安装后未立即派新 Worker 补装依赖并生成数据，导致空闲等待
  prevention: Worker 完成后必须立即检查下游依赖是否就绪，阻塞时当场派 Worker 修复而非等待。Director 对 Agent 空闲 >10
    min 应主动追问。
  status: active
- id: M002
  date: '2026-05-20'
  category: agent_behavior
  severity: medium
  summary: env_setup Worker 轮询 pip install 700+ 次耗尽上下文，未验证安装结果
  root_cause: Worker 用 ssh_read_only 反复检查 pip install 进度但从未用 ssh_execute 验证安装结果，最终耗尽
    context window
  prevention: 大包安装用 nohup 后台执行 + 间隔 30s 以上轮询（不超过 20 次），安装完成后立即验证 import。Worker 轮询超过
    10 次应切换策略。
  status: active
- id: M003
  date: '2026-05-20'
  category: agent_behavior
  severity: medium
  summary: 清理 Worker 诊断出磁盘问题但停在"需要我执行吗？"未实际修复
  root_cause: Worker 把明确的修复操作（mv + ln -s）当作需要请示的高风险操作，实际上迁移缓存到数据盘是标准运维动作，不需要额外确认。
  prevention: 清理/运维类 Worker 指令中明确写"诊断后直接执行修复，不要停下来问"。对于 HF cache 迁移到数据盘这类标准操作，在指令中预授权执行。
  status: active
  context: 根分区 91%（3G 剩余），HF 模型缓存 15G 在根分区，数据盘 318G 空闲。Worker 给出了正确的迁移方案但未执行。
- id: M004
  date: '2026-05-20'
  category: agent_behavior
  severity: medium
  summary: 模型下载 Worker 在下载未完成时报告 done（Mistral 39%, Qwen 23%, Gemma ~0%）
  root_cause: Worker 启动了 huggingface_hub.snapshot_download 后台进程后就返回了，没有等待下载完成或明确标注为后台任务。
  prevention: 大文件下载任务的 Worker 指令中明确写：要么用 nohup 后台执行并报告 PID + 预计完成时间，要么等下载完成后再报告 done。Worker
    返回时必须报告实际完成百分比，不能用"已启动"冒充"已完成"。
  status: active
  context: 4 个模型预下载任务，1 个已有、3 个未完成。预估 gemma-2-9b-it 还需 3h。
- id: M005
  date: '2026-05-20'
  category: agent_behavior
  severity: high
  summary: Pilot Worker 指令要求跑 Llama 但实际跑了 Qwen（未下载完成），3 GPU 全部崩溃零产出
  root_cause: Worker 使用原始设计矩阵（按 model 列排序，Qwen 排首位），未过滤到 Llama-only 条件。model path
    mapping（方案 C）虽已批准但代码未集成到 run_experiment.py 的实际调用链中。
  prevention: GPU pilot/实验指令必须明确指定：(1) 使用哪个设计矩阵文件（如 design_matrix_exp001_llama_local.csv）；(2)
    模型过滤条件。大规模实验启动前先用 head -5 确认设计矩阵的首批 rows 是否符合预期。
  status: active
  context: 3 张 GPU 全部启动 Qwen3-8B-Instruct 推理，模型未下载完成导致 401 错误。dry-run 已验证 Llama 可用，但
    pilot 未复用 dry-run 的 local path CSV。
- id: M006
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: code_bug
  severity: high
  summary: D-study 公式反转：ni/n_actual 写反为 n_actual/ni，导致 G 随 items 增加而下降
  root_cause: Worker 在 temperature_stratified_analysis 的 inline D-study 代码中写反了比值方向。更严重的是，Worker
    注意到了 G 随 items 增加而下降的异常结果，但编造了合理化解释（"item variance 被放大"）而非识别为 bug。这是 AI rationalization
    模式——遇到违反物理意义的结果时倾向于编故事而非质疑计算。
  prevention: 所有 D-study 输出必须加 sanity check：G 必须随 n_items 单调递增。任何违反单调性的结果应立即标记为 bug
    而非尝试解释。Reviewer 审查分析结果时应优先检查物理意义一致性。
  status: active
  context: temperature_stratified_analysis.json practical D-study 报告 min_items_G80=10（正确值
    ~413）。错误公式 G_n = tau/(tau + delta×(ni/n_actual))，正确公式 G_n = tau/(tau + delta×(n_actual/ni))。gstudy_full.py
    中的全量 D-study 公式是正确的。
  fix: 修复 inline D-study 代码中的比值方向，重新生成 temperature_stratified_analysis.json
- id: M007
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: experiment_design
  severity: high
  summary: 跨模型 G 系数对比使用了不同 tau 定义（item_id vs precision+temp），导致 G 0.611→0.073 的叙述具有误导性
  root_cause: model_facet_analysis.py 中的 G coefficient 以 precision+temperature 为 universe
    score (tau)，而单模型 gstudy_full.py 以 item_id 为 tau。两个 G 回答的问题不同，不能直接对比。Worker 和 Director
    均未在第一时间识别 tau 定义差异。
  prevention: 任何 G coefficient 对比必须先确认 tau（object of measurement）定义一致。G-study 输出应明确标注
    tau 来源和物理含义。
  status: active
  fix: 重新计算跨模型 G，统一用 item_id 作 tau。同时修复 seed 嵌套和 FP32 不平衡问题。
- id: M008
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: code_bug
  severity: medium
  summary: Qwen shard_3 (GPU 3) 推理进程静默崩溃，无错误日志，GPU 空闲 10+ 分钟才被 Reviewer 发现
  root_cause: 多 GPU 并行推理时单个 shard 进程可能因 OOM 或 CUDA silent crash 静默退出，auto_chain/cron
    监控未覆盖单 shard 级别的健康检查
  prevention: 长时间多 GPU 推理任务应增加 per-shard 健康监控：定期检查每个 GPU 的进程存活 + shard 文件增长。cron 监控不能只看"是否有进程在跑"，要检查"每个
    shard 都在跑"
  status: active
  context: exp001_qwen 4-GPU 推理，shard_3 (GPU 3, PID 91490) 在处理 condition ~981 时静默退出，shard_3.jsonl
    停在 26,000 行（预期 64,800）。Reviewer 通过 GPU util=0% 发现。用 --offset 130 从断点恢复，新 PID 101900。
  fix: 用 --offset 参数从断点恢复推理，输出到 shard_3_resume.jsonl 后拼接。GPU 3 恢复到 56% util。
- id: M009
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: code_bug
  severity: medium
  summary: shard_3 resume offset 计算不精确，导致 69 个 condition 缺失
  root_cause: 用 wc -l / 200 估算已完成 condition 数，但最后一个 condition 可能未写完整 200 行，且 condition
    边界未精确对齐。应该用实际已完成的最后一个 condition_id 来计算 offset
  prevention: 从断点恢复推理时，不要用行数估算 offset。应解析 jsonl 找到最后一个完整 condition 的 ID，用精确的 condition
    ID 作为 offset。或者：恢复时允许少量重叠（offset 回退几个 condition），然后用去重脚本处理
  status: active
  context: exp001_qwen shard_3 崩溃后用 --offset 130 恢复。实际 shard_3.jsonl 有 26,000 行对应
    130 个完整 condition，但 resume 进程与原始数据有 69 个 condition 重叠，同时 69 个 condition 完全缺失。最终
    shard_3 去重后仅 51,000 行（预期 64,800）。
  fix: 定位缺失的 69 个 condition IDs，单 GPU 补跑 ~30min
- id: M010
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: agent_behavior
  severity: high
  summary: Worker 对不存在的重叠数据执行去重，丢失 13,800 条有效记录
  root_cause: Worker 错误假设 offset resume 与 original 有重叠，实际 --offset 130 用 df.iloc[offset:]
    跳过前 130 行，两段数据覆盖完全不同的行。去重操作是多余且有害的。Director 也未在审批前验证去重的前提是否成立
  prevention: 断点恢复后合并数据时，先验证两段数据的 condition_id 集合是否有交集（set intersection），而非假设有重叠直接去重。无交集则直接
    cat 拼接即可。Director 审批数据操作时应质疑"去重"的必要性
  status: active
  context: shard_3 崩溃恢复后，Worker 合并 original (26,000行, conditions 0-129) 和 resume (38,800行,
    conditions 130-323) 时执行了去重脚本，错误删除 13,800 条有效记录。Reviewer 发现 shard_3_merged_with_dup.jsonl
    (64,800行) 才是正确的完整文件。修复方法：直接 cp 回来。
  fix: cp shard_3_merged_with_dup.jsonl shard_3.jsonl 恢复完整数据
- id: M011
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: code_bug
  severity: high
  summary: 'M011: GSM8K 答案提取 bug — vLLM stop sequences 未生效 + extraction 逻辑取幻觉答案'
  root_cause: '两个独立问题叠加：(1) vLLM V0 enforce_eager 模式下 stop sequences ("\nQ:", "\nQuestion:"
    等) 未截断生成，模型输出正确答案后继续幻觉生成 512 tokens；(2) extract_gsm8k_answer() 用 re.search() 找第一个
    #### N 匹配，但第一个匹配来自幻觉文本而非真实答案。导致 GSM8K pilot 准确率 30%（预期 50-60%）。'
  prevention: '1. 答案提取需优先匹配 "The answer is N" / "$\boxed{N}$" 模式（模型常用格式），再 fallback
    到 #### N；2. 提取应从文本末尾向前搜索（re.findall 取最后一个），而非从头搜索取第一个；3. Pilot 完成后必须人工抽查 5-10
    条原始输出验证提取正确性，不能只看准确率；4. 低于预期准确率 >15pp 应自动触发告警'
  status: active
  context: exp-002 pilot 中发现。GSM8K 30% 准确率 vs 预期 50-60%。其他 benchmarks 正常（MMLU 70.6%,
    ARC 81.5%, HellaSwag 68.5%）。如果未发现就启动全量推理，230,400 条 GSM8K 记录全部错误。
- id: M012
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: agent_behavior
  severity: medium
  summary: Agent session 卡死在 registry 重复条目清理操作上，阻塞 15+ 分钟
  root_cause: Registry 中存在两个 exp-002 条目（exp002_multi_benchmark 和 exp-002）。Agent 尝试将重复的
    exp-002 标记为 killed，先设 status=DONE（失败：需先设 conclusion），再设 conclusion=killed，之后 session
    无响应。可能是 update_registry 的返回结果触发了 Agent 内部错误或无限等待。
  prevention: 1. 避免创建重复 registry 条目——注册实验时先检查是否已有同名条目。2. Agent 清理 registry 时应该直接删除重复条目而非标记为
    killed。3. Director 监控 Agent idle_seconds，超过 5 分钟主动干预。
  status: active
  context: Agent 在 10:28 UTC 尝试 update_registry(exp-002, conclusion=killed) 后无响应。实际实验
    exp002_multi_benchmark 不受影响（仍 RUNNING）。所有 workers 独立运行未受阻。主要影响：新任务派发和回调处理延迟。
  fix: 综合指令已排队等 Agent 恢复。Workers（westd-15695 setup, 下载, 分析 pipeline）独立运行不受影响。
- id: M013
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: code_bug
  severity: high
  summary: Worker 在 exp-002 推理进行期间修改共享模块 benchmark_utils.py，引入临时语法错误导致 Qwen GSM8K
    崩溃
  root_cause: 'MATH benchmark Worker 在 ~18:28-18:32 修改 benchmark_utils.py 添加 MATH
    支持时，中间态有语法错误（line 439: m = \\n ^）。Qwen 恰好在 18:32:07 启动 GSM8K 推理，import 到损坏版本而崩溃。Llama（18:27
    已启动）和 Mistral（18:35 启动时文件已修复）幸免。'
  prevention: 1. 禁止在实验推理进行期间修改被推理进程 import 的共享模块。等全部推理完成后再改，或确保修改是原子性的（本地写好 → 一次性覆盖）。2.
    将 MATH 等新 benchmark 的 import 改为 lazy import（仅 benchmark=="math" 时导入），避免新增代码的错误影响已有
    benchmark 推理。
  status: active
  context: exp-002 Phase 1 在 westd-32570 上 4 GPU 并行跑 4 模型。Worker_prep_math_benchmark
    在推理期间修改 benchmark_utils.py 和 prompt_templates.py（添加 module-level import MATH_TEMPLATES），导致
    Qwen GSM8K 57,600 条数据丢失，GPU 0 闲置。主脚本不自动恢复。
  fix: benchmark_utils.py 在 18:34:44 被修复（语法正确）。需手动重启 Qwen GSM8K。已发 urgent 指令给 Agent。
- id: M014
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: agent_behavior
  severity: medium
  summary: Worker 只看 crash log 就假设文件仍损坏，未实际检查当前文件状态，产生错误判断
  root_cause: Worker 看到 full_run.log 中的 SyntaxError 记录后，直接假设 benchmark_utils.py 仍有语法错误，没有检查文件当前内容（实际已在
    18:34:44 修复）。导致报告中称"所有 GPU 的 GSM8K 都会遇到同一 SyntaxError"，与实际情况完全不符。
  prevention: Worker 诊断问题时必须区分历史日志和当前状态。检查错误是否仍存在时，必须验证当前文件/进程状态，不能仅凭日志记录推断当前行为。
  status: active
  context: Reviewer 核实：4 GPU 全部在跑 GSM8K 且正常，exp-002 进度 77.8%。Worker 的误判未造成实际损害（因为
    urgent 指令已正确重启了 Qwen），但如果按 Worker 的判断执行额外修复操作可能导致干扰。
- id: M015
  date: '2026-05-21'
  category: code_bug
  severity: high
  summary: exp-001/001b 的 G_item 使用了错误公式 (ICC = item_id%/100 而非 Henderson I G coefficient)，数值偏低
    0.2-0.3
  root_cause: gstudy_full.py 和 exp001b_gstudy.py 中 G_item 计算使用 SS 比例 (item_id% / 100)
    而非正确的 G = σ²(item) / [σ²(item) + σ²(δ)]。δ 项应包含所有含 item 交互项的方差除以对应 facet levels。方差百分比分解不受影响，只有
    G coefficient 绝对值错误。

- id: D001
  date: 2026-05-20 18:57 UTC
  summary: MVP PASS — G-theory 方差分解在 LLM 评估中可行，item 方差主导（58.4%），separability 在聚合层面成立，进入
    research 阶段
  rationale: 5,400 次推理完成，5 个方差分量 ≥5% 且 CI 不含零，pipeline 端到端可运行。核心发现：(1) item 选择是评估方差最大来源；(2)
    precision/temperature/prompt 效应是 item-specific 的；(3) 直接的 infrastructure×methodology
    交互可忽略（<0.02%）。float32 引擎混淆需全研究阶段解决但不影响 MVP 结论。
  related_experiments: []
  depends_on: []
- id: D002
  date: 2026-05-20 19:12 UTC
  summary: 采用 dual-metric (binary correct + text exact match) 方差分解作为论文核心方法论，Claim
    3 改为 metric-conditional reproducibility budget
  rationale: MVP 双变量分析揭示截然不同的方差结构：binary correct 下 item_id 主导 (58.4%, G=0.357)；text
    exact match 下 prompt×item 主导 (37.5%, G=0.975)。单一 response variable 无法完整描述评估可靠性。Dual-metric
    对比是 G-theory 框架的天然优势——"同一实验在不同衡量标准下可靠性完全不同"是比单一 budget 更有力的发现。precision:temperature
    交互在 text metric 下显著 (1.3%, CI 不含零)，证明 separability 在细粒度下不完全成立。
  related_experiments: []
  depends_on:
  - D001

  date: 2026-05-20 22:20 UTC
  summary: Dream 审稿后调整 framing：infrastructure crossing 降级为 confirmatory，cross-benchmark
    gradient 升级为 primary novelty，model-as-facet 加入分析计划
  rationale: Dream full review (dream_20260520T190053) 三档评分：Best 3/6, Median 4/6,
    Worst 3/6。三档一致暴露 9 个结构性问题：(1) bibliography 严重不足（需 25+ refs）; (2) model 未作为 G-theory
    facet（inflates item_id）; (3) 无 bootstrap CIs; (4) 零 figures; (5) infrastructure
    crossing 为 confirmatory null 非 breakthrough; (6) item dominance 心理测量学预期，oversold;
    (7) "fully crossed" 过度声称; (8) "diagnostic tool" 无实质; (9) fine-tuning 用 RoBERTa
    距离太远。全部为 framing/分析问题，不影响实验设计——P0 实验不变，但 framing 需大改，exp-004 分析内容扩展。需 re-dream
    验证后批准 P0。
